name: Biriba
description: Biriba (Μπιρίμπα) is Greece's most popular card game, a rich and strategic partnership rummy game. Played with two decks and four Jokers, it challenges players to form sets and runs, including at least one 'biriba' (a 7-card meld), to go out. The game is famous for its 'pot' mechanic, where players pick up a reserve hand once they empty their initial deal. It combines the deep calculation of Burraco with the high-speed timing of Canasta.

overview.description: Biriba (Μπιρίμπα) is Greece's most popular card game, a rich and strategic partnership rummy game. Played with two decks and four Jokers, it challenges players to form sets and runs, including at least one 'biriba' (a 7-card meld), to go out. history.origins: Believed to be derived from Italian Burraco or early Canasta variants, Biriba developed into a unique national pastime in Greece and Cyprus during the mid-20th century. It is a staple of Greek coffeehouse (kafeneia) culture.
timeline: 1950s: Rummy variants like Burraco spread through the Mediterranean.
1970s: Biriba becomes the dominant social game in urban Greek centers.
Present: Remains the standard social game for Greek families and clubs, with numerous online implementations.
history.cultural: An essential part of Greek hospitality and social life, often played during holidays or extended cafe visits.
history.evolution: Greek house rules added layers like the 'bonus suit' and specific discard-capture requirements that distinguish it from standard Burraco.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: 108 cards: Two standard 52-card decks plus four Jokers. Jokers and 2s are wild.
setup.dealing: Deal 11 cards to each player. Two 'pots' (reserve hands) of 11 cards each are placed face down. Remaining cards form the stock.
setup.equipment: Standard pack with jokers, score pad.

rules.objective: Score points through melds and go out. You must complete at least one 'biriba' (meld of 7+ cards) to be eligible to go out.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Draw**: Take from stock or pick up the entire discard pile (if the top card is immediately melded). 2. **Meld**: Place sets (same rank) or runs (same suit sequence) on the table. 3. **Discard**: End turn by placing one card face up on the pile. 4. **Pot**: The first player to empty their hand takes the first 'pot' hand. 5. **End**: Round ends when a player with at least one biriba empties their hand again.
keyRules: Clean Biriba (no wilds) = 500 pts. Dirty Biriba (with wilds) = 300 pts.
Cards left in hand are negative points.

strategy.basic: Focus on clearing your initial 11 cards quickly to grab the 'pot' before the opponents. Don't worry about clean biribas until you have your second hand.
strategy.intermediate: Discard Pile Management: If the pile contains cards that help your runs, wait for it to grow large before capturing it. Conversely, discard 'poison' cards that don't help opponents.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Melding: Don't lay down your melds too early if they reveal your strategy to the opponents. Keep components in hand until you can complete a 7-card biriba in one move.
tips: Always track how many Jokers and 2s have been played.
Prioritize runs over sets, as runs are easier to extend into clean biribas.

variations.name: Runs Only (No Sets)
variations.description: Only suit sequences are allowed; rank-based sets are prohibited, making the game much harder.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation changes only allowed meld types; no engine constants or numeric parameters differ from the base rules.

scoring.description: Clean biriba = 500, Dirty biriba = 300, Going out = 100. Card values: Joker 20, 2s 10, Aces 15, 8-K 10, 3-7 5, matching the standard Pagat rules. Cards left in hand are subtracted.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach target score (typically 2,500 or 5,000 points).

synthesis.shortDescription: The most popular card game in Greece. A rich partnership rummy where you build sets and runs, race to complete 7-card 'biribas', and grab reserve hands from the pot. Two decks, four Jokers, endless strategy. Clean biribas score 500; dirty ones 300. First team to the target wins.
